title: Outcome Under Seal: one complete pass, zero borrowed preferences

ciFast.note: The exact v0.16.18 content commit must pass Fast verification on GitHub before the release proof is finalized.

ciDeep.note: This release contains one atom-level Codex order. It does not claim the required fresh reverse-order pass, a stable preference corpus, adapter training, held-out adapter quality, or a browser-device matrix.

deploy.note: GitHub Pages and the cache-busted edutool.dev release surfaces must be verified after the content commit reaches main.

liveProvider.note: The milestone judges already retained anonymous atom artifacts and changes no hosted model, provider route, public base, adapter, or inference weights.

manualHuman.note: The declared training lane is single-model Codex evidence. No human, instructor, independent, classroom, or multi-judge claim is made or required.

strictLayeredEvaluation.note: The strict general release profile correctly refuses a classroom-quality claim: independently validated held-out cases and completed independent instructor reviews are both zero. Codex evidence does not substitute for either tier.

claims.summary: Training review v2 presents the exact neutral source to the judge and uses a hash-bound atom prompt that excludes unsupported full-course and operational constructs.
The validator and ingestion path preserve winner, tie, insufficient-evidence, order-sensitive, and below-floor outcomes instead of manufacturing training winners.
One isolated A/B Codex session completed all 128 source-backed cases and passed structural validation with exact packet, prompt, source, artifact, scorecard, decision, and session bindings.

The complete pass is retained only as an AES-256-GCM envelope whose plaintext, ciphertext, key, packet, prompt, and judge identities are hash-bound; template regeneration preserves evidence, and two 0600 untracked local keys passed an exact round trip without disclosing an outcome in Git.
The missing B/A context keeps stable preferences, qualifying quality-training rows, learned adapter weights, and adapter/model wins at zero; public Scion remains base-only.
